Compute Shapley variable contributions for a local counterfactual

bl_shapley.Rd

Explains which variables drive the prediction from the observed point to the boundary counterfactual using Shapley values. For \(p \le\) exact_max_vars variables, the exact formula is used; otherwise a permutation approximation is applied.

Usage

bl_shapley(
  bl_local_result,
  exact_max_vars = 14L,
  approx_perm = 2048L,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

bl_local_result

A "bl_local_result" object produced by bl_find_local_cf.

exact_max_vars

Integer; use exact computation when the number of variables is at most this value. Default 14L.

approx_perm

Integer; number of permutations for the approximate method. Default 2048L.

seed

Random seed for the approximate method. NULL (default) uses the current RNG state, giving independent estimates across repeated calls. Supply an integer (e.g. 1L) for reproducible results.

Value

A list of class "bl_shapley" with the following fields:

shapley_df

Data frame; one row per variable, sorted by contribution, with columns varnames, pred_data, data_to_boundary, shapley_cause, pred_use, Contribute, varnames_p.

pred_prob

Scalar predicted probability of the target.

pred_class

Integer predicted class of the target.

pred_boundary

Scalar predicted probability at the boundary.

row_id

Integer row ID, or NA_integer_ for external data.

bl_local_result

The "bl_local_result" passed in.

Details

The Contribute column in the returned data frame classifies each variable as "Supports" (pushes the prediction toward the boundary) or "Contradicts" (pushes it away from the boundary).
